QUAD 306 · POWER AMPLIFIER

Restoring your Quad 306

The Quad 306 is a compact power amplifier, about 50 watts per channel. It drives your loudspeakers and works well with Quad preamps such as the 34 and 44.

This guide is new. Nobody has checked its parts list against a real Quad 306 yet, so treat it as a starting point.

Before anything else: stay safe

This power amplifier plugs into the mains. Parts inside can still give you a dangerous shock after it is unplugged.

If you are new to electronics, don't open it. You can do everything on this page from the outside. A qualified technician does the work inside.

Four steps

1

Write down a few details

You can find all of these from the outside.

  • The serial number.
  • Your preamplifier, and whether the 306 is used together with a 606 to drive one pair of speakers.
  • Anything already done to it.
2

Talk it through with an AI assistant

An AI assistant with the Quad Agent guide checks your details against Quad's own documents and tells you what applies to your Quad 306. It asks questions first and never guesses part values.

Copy this into your AI assistant:

Read quad-upgrade/SKILL.md and follow it to help me restore my Quad 306. Start by helping me identify it from the outside.

It needs the guide files first. Download the guide and add it to your assistant, or give it the quad-upgrade folder.

3

Choose what you want done

The recap

A recap replaces the ageing capacitors, including the two big ones that store power. DADA's kit also updates a few input parts the way Quad later did on the 606 MK II.

Optional extras

These change how the Quad 306 behaves. You don't need any of them.

  • Lower sensitivity. The 306 is very sensitive as standard. Changing one resistor makes the volume control easier to use with most preamps. Skip it if the 306 is used alongside a 606.
4

Take it to a technician

Send them the link to this page. Everything they need is in the section below: the parts list, Quad's service documents and the upgrade guides.

Ask them to check the parts against your actual Quad 306 before ordering. Quad changed things during production, and earlier owners may have too.

Good to know

  • If the 306 cuts out after 10 to 20 seconds of very loud test tone, that is its protection working. It is normal.
  • The output transistors have small pink paint dots. If they have turned purple, the transistors have overheated and a technician should check them.
  • New loudspeaker terminals go in the order red, black, black, red.
